clue.text: Game to sell up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up tells the solver to read the word for selling from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to flog is slang for to sell

explanation.surface: Someone decides to cash in on a game they own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FLOG over in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport played with clubs on a course is one example of a game.

clue.text: See 26
Just one introduced to smallholding, certainly not English

indicators.note: one piece is put into the middle of the other, as something is introduced into a place

parts.note: a smallholding is a small farm
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the letter for English is left out, so it is not there

parts.note: indeed is an emphatic word for certainly

explanation.surface: A fair-minded newcomer joins a small farm, and is emphatically not English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced to' puts I into FARM to give FAIRM; 'not' removes the E from INDEED, leaving INDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone just is fair and impartial in their judgements, a synonym of the hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Sinful trade, penny-pinching if 19 down

definitions.meaning: the buying and selling of church offices or pardons, a sin in church law
19 down is BELOW PAR: put the entry below the letters PAR and you get a word for meanness with money

explanation.surface: Trading in holy favours is sinful, and stingy too.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the puzzle's golf-themed clues: 'if 19 down' asks you to write PAR above the answer, so PAR plus the answer makes PARSIMONY, penny-pinching.
explanation.definitionFit: Simony is the medieval sin of trading in church posts or sacred things for money.

clue.text: Wave painted with minimum of ebb, suggesting this?

definitions.text: Wave painted with minimum of ebb, suggesting this?

indicators.note: to wave can mean to move to and fro, so the letters are stirred into a new order
the least part of the word ebb, its first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: A painting of a wave at low water seems to depict a particular tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' shuffles PAINTED plus E, the first letter of 'ebb' picked by 'minimum of'. The whole clue also defines: the tide with the least range.
explanation.definitionFit: A neap tide is the tide with the smallest range, a picture of a sea at its minimum.

clue.text: Fit relation, if 19 down

definitions.meaning: ... to do something, capable or fit for it
19 down is BELOW PAR: with PAR written above the entry, the word formed is a story, a relation in the sense of a narrative

explanation.surface: A healthy relative, provided they are feeling under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf theme: put PAR above the answer and PARABLE, a told story or 'relation', appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Being capable or competent is the sense of fit that matches this adjective.

clue.text: Whip good amid pleasure as photographer's aid

indicators.note: these letters sit in the middle of the word for pleasure

parts.note: fun is a synonym of pleasure
to lash is to whip

explanation.surface: Whipping and enjoyment are odd things to find in a camera kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' looks like the definition but is just a verb to lash; 'amid' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashgun is the device that provides a burst of light for a camera.

clue.text: Appear menacing in reception room, if 19 down

definitions.meaning: to look dark and threatening, as a sky or a frowning person
19 down is BELOW PAR: with PAR written above the entry, the word formed is a sitting room for receiving guests

explanation.surface: Someone looks threatening in the front room while feeling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf theme: PAR placed above the answer gives PARLOUR, a reception room.
explanation.definitionFit: To lour (or lower) is to scowl or look dark and threatening, like a stormy sky.

clue.text: Old musical players making comeback in effect

indicators.note: a comeback turns the run of words backwards, so both pieces are read from the end

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Peron
rep, short for repertory company, is a group of theatre players

explanation.surface: An old stage show and its cast return to the theatre to good effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' turns both pieces together, giving PERATIVE after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A law that is operative is in force, which is the same as being in effect.

clue.text: South African martyr hugs liberal sergeant on TV

indicators.note: one word wraps its arms round the other, so it goes outside

parts.note: Steve Biko was the anti-apartheid activist who died in police custody in 1977

explanation.surface: A political martyr embraces a liberal and a television sergeant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugs' puts L inside BIKO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeant Ernie Bilko was the scheming army sergeant of the US sitcom The Phil Silvers Show.

clue.text: Muslim ascetic having a weekend in tree

indicators.note: the letters are placed inside the name of the tree

parts.note: a fir is a conifer
the end of the word week is its last letter, K

explanation.surface: A holy man spends a weekend up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and K inside FIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A fakir is a Muslim (or Hindu) holy man who lives by begging and self-denial.

clue.text: Pole thus imprisoned by proper sort of tyrant

indicators.note: these letters are locked up inside the others
to sort letters is to rearrange them

parts.note: S, south, is one of the poles
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A Polish man is jailed by a correct kind of tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is not a Polish person but S; 'sort of' shuffles the word proper and 'imprisoned by' locks the two short pieces inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An oppressor rules harshly and unjustly, as a tyrant does.

clue.text: Oxford and Cambridge differ about rest

indicators.note: one word goes round the other

parts.note: to vary is to differ
to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: The two old universities disagree about having a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. The Varsity match is the annual contest between Oxford and Cambridge universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Varsity, old slang for university, is used for things involving both Oxford and Cambridge, like the Varsity match.

clue.text: Goddess taking new arrivals, if 19 down

definitions.meaning: 19 down is BELOW PAR: with PAR written above the entry, the word formed means upstarts, people who have recently risen in society

explanation.surface: A goddess welcomes newcomers while out of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf theme: PAR above the answer makes PARVENUS, social upstarts or new arrivals. 'taking' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus was the Roman goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: 22 down one 19 down, we hear? But that's out of bounds

indicators.note: says the words are said out loud and heard as another word

parts.note: 22 down is a bird and 19 down means sick, so a sick bird, one that in golf terms is two under par, gives ill eagle

explanation.surface: A sick bird is something the rules forbid, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf an eagle is two under par; an ill eagle said out loud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of bounds is forbidden or not permitted, as an unlawful act is.

clue.text: Thrashing tail of salmon tangled in angler's equipment

indicators.note: a thrashing fish throws itself about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the tail of the word salmon is its last letter

explanation.surface: A thrashing salmon gets caught up in the fisherman's gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrashing' shuffles N (the last letter of salmon, from 'tail of') with TANGLED and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing net is used by an angler to lift a hooked fish out of the water.

clue.text: Weapon, as one might say, if 19 down

definitions.meaning: a long spear carried by a mounted knight

definitions.text: as one might say, if 19 down
definitions.meaning: 19 down is BELOW PAR: with PAR written above the entry, the word formed means a way of speaking or idiom

explanation.surface: A weapon, so to speak, for anyone below their best.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf theme: PAR above the answer makes PARLANCE, a manner of speaking, as in 'in common parlance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear used by a horseman, a classic weapon.

clue.text: Rover never barking

parts.note: no can mean never, as in 'no way'
barking is British slang for mad

explanation.surface: A dog called Rover that never barks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rover' looks like a dog's name to go with 'barking', but it means a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is a wanderer, which is what a nomad is.

clue.text: Vegetarian's order is terribly late in canteen

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are put inside the word for a canteen

parts.note: a mess is a military canteen or dining hall

indicators.note: terribly signals that the word late is badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A vegetarian's meal in the canteen arrives very late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' gives EATL, and 'in' places it inside the canteen word.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetarian orders food without meat, so the order is a meatless one.

clue.text: Run past in discussion

indicators.note: in discussion means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: by means past, as in 'walk by'

explanation.surface: Someone runs past while a conversation is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batsman without being hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bye is a run in cricket scored without the batsman touching the ball.

clue.text: Tungsten absorbed by cut in stomach making sick …

indicators.note: the inner pieces go inside the word for stomach

parts.note: to stomach something is to bear it

indicators.note: the chemical symbol is soaked up inside the word for cut

parts.note: to lop is to cut
W is the chemical symbol for tungsten

explanation.surface: A heavy metal swallowed after a stomach cut makes someone ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed by' gives LOWP and 'in' places that inside the stomach word; 'stomach' is a verb here, meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling under the weather or below one's usual standard is a mild way of saying sick.

clue.text: Thespian finally acquainted with material

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to be in on something is to know about it

explanation.surface: An actor at last gets to know some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes N from 'Thespian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a light, sheer fabric of silk or nylon, so it is a material.

clue.text: Hundred resident in shoe — shame!

indicators.note: the letter lives inside the word for the shoe

parts.note: a sandal is a kind of shoe
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Finding a hundred stashed in a shoe is a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resident in' places C inside SANDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a disgraceful event, and shame is the cry of outrage it provokes.

clue.text: Interjection from Scotsman tucking into cheese roll

indicators.note: the exclamation goes inside the cheese, as a diner tucks into food

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
och is a Scottish exclamation

explanation.surface: A Scot exclaims while tucking into a cheese roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' signals the container; 'roll' is the bread, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a soft, sweet bread roll.

clue.text: … as a parrot, perhaps

parts.note: continuing 19 down, read 'below par as a parrot': the golf score of one under par, which is also a pet word for a bird such as a parrot

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, someone is sick as a parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 19 down: 'sick as a parrot' is a British phrase for very disappointed. In golf this score is one under par.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdie is a childish word for any bird, a parrot for example, and the golf score one below par.

clue.text: Quick constable's first to join force

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a lever applies force, and to lever is to force open

explanation.surface: A policeman joins the force and proves sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes C from 'constable's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in the sense of quick-witted means clever or bright.

clue.text: Drive softly into tree in front of sovereign

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second
the letter goes inside the tree's name

parts.note: willow is a tree
p (piano) is the musical direction for softly
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch's cipher

explanation.surface: A car is driven gently into a tree in front of the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts P into WILLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive in the sense of determination or resolve is a synonym.

clue.text: See 26
Tear skin

definitions.meaning: to rush along at speed, to tear

explanation.definitionFit: Pelt means both to tear along fast and an animal's skin with the fur on.

clue.text: Target in 1 club, spirits kept up to achieve 22 down

parts.note: 1 down is golf, where the green is the target with the hole
a wood is a golf club
keep your pecker up is a British phrase for keep your spirits up, so pecker means spirits

explanation.surface: A golfer aims for the green with a club, keeping cheerful to make a birdie.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down here means bird. 'Keep your pecker up' is British slang for 'stay cheerful'. 'to achieve' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The green woodpecker is a common British bird.

clue.text: 22 down's place reliable, though no house

indicators.note: no house means the abbreviation for house is taken out

parts.note: honest means trustworthy, reliable

explanation.surface: A bird's home is dependable, though it is not a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes HO from HONEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird lives and lays its eggs in the structure it builds, its home.

clue.text: 22 down by river and lake

parts.note: the Ouse is the name of several English rivers

explanation.surface: A bird sits beside a river and a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An ousel (ouzel) is a bird, the old name for the blackbird or ring ouzel.

clue.text: Existing quality in a vessel at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: Life aboard a ship out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' shuffles IN A VESSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being alive is the quality of existing.
